connectorUiConfig.title: Databricks Audit Logs via Amazon S3 (via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown:
Ingests the account and workspace audit logs that [Databricks on AWS](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/audit-logs) delivers to an Amazon S3 bucket. Microsoft Sentinel polls an Amazon SQS queue for new objects, reads them from S3 with an IAM role it assumes through OpenID Connect, and writes one row per audit event to the **DatabricksAudit_CL** table through a data collection rule. No code runs in your subscription and no AWS access keys are stored.

Azure Databricks is not covered by this connector; it writes to Log Analytics through diagnostic settings.

sampleQueries.description: Failed logins by source IP, last 24 hours
sampleQueries.query:
{{graphQueriesTableName}}
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ServiceName == "accounts" and ActionName has "login" and ResponseStatusCode >= 400
| summarize Failures = count(), Users = make_set(UserEmail, 20) by SourceIPAddress, WorkspaceId
| order by Failures desc

sampleQueries.description: Events by service and action, last 7 days
sampleQueries.query:
{{graphQueriesTableName}}
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| summarize Events = count() by ServiceName, ActionName
| order by Events desc

dataTypes.name: {{graphQueriesTableName}}
dataTypes.lastDataReceivedQuery:
{{graphQueriesTableName}}
| where TimeGenerated > ago(12h)
| summarize Time = max(TimeGenerated)
| where isnotempty(Time)

customs.name: Databricks
customs.description: A Databricks account on the Premium or Enterprise tier with audit log delivery to Amazon S3 configured (log type AUDIT_LOGS, output format JSON).

customs.name: AWS
customs.description: Permission to create an IAM role and OpenID Connect provider, an SQS queue, and an S3 bucket notification in the account that holds the Databricks delivery bucket.

parameters.content:
### 1. Databricks: deliver audit logs to S3
In the Databricks account console, configure audit log delivery with `log_type` **AUDIT_LOGS**, `output_format` **JSON** and a `delivery_path_prefix`. Databricks writes objects to `<prefix>/workspaceId=<id>/date=<yyyy-mm-dd>/auditlogs_<id>.json`, one JSON object per line. Confirm with `aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/` that `workspaceId=` folders exist before continuing.

### 2. AWS: identity provider, role, queue and notification
Deploy the two CloudFormation templates from the solution's `Data Connectors/CloudFormationTemplates` folder in the [AWS CloudFormation console](https://aka.ms/awsCloudFormationLink#/stacks/create), or run `aws/setup-aws.sh` from the companion package.

1. **OIDCWebIdProvider.json**: the OpenID Connect provider for Microsoft Sentinel. Skip it if another Microsoft Sentinel AWS connector already created it in this account.
2. **DatabricksAuditLogsResources.json**: the IAM role (name must start with `OIDC_`), the SQS queue and dead-letter queue, and the queue policy. Enter the Workspace ID below as the `SentinelWorkspaceId` parameter and the Databricks bucket and prefix as `BucketName` and `DeliveryPathPrefix`.
3. If the bucket already exists (the usual case, since Databricks writes to it), add an **ObjectCreated** event notification on the bucket to the queue the stack created, filtered on the prefix. The template does this for you only when it creates the bucket.

Note the **Role ARN** and **Queue URL** from the stack outputs.

### 3. Connect new collectors
Click **Add new collector**, paste the Role ARN and the Queue URL, and click **Connect**. Rows appear in the table within 5 to 15 minutes of the next object being written to S3. Objects already in the bucket are not read.

dataFlows.transformKql: source | extend EventTime = unixtime_milliseconds_todatetime(timestamp) | extend TimeGenerated = iff(EventTime between ((now() - 47h) .. (now() + 10m)), EventTime, now()) | extend ResponseStatusCode = toint(response.statusCode) | project TimeGenerated, EventTime, SchemaVersion = version, AuditLevel = auditLevel, AccountId = accountId, OrgId = tostring(orgId), WorkspaceId = iff(isempty(workspaceId), tostring(orgId), workspaceId), ShardName = shardName, ServiceName = serviceName, ActionName = actionName, RequestId = requestId, SessionId = sessionId, SourceIPAddress = sourceIPAddress, UserAgent = userAgent, UserEmail = tostring(userIdentity.email), UserSubjectName = tostring(userIdentity.subjectName), UserIdentity = userIdentity, RequestParams = requestParams, ResponseStatusCode, ResponseErrorMessage = tostring(response.errorMessage), ResponseResult = response.result, S3Bucket = '', S3Key = ''

columns.name: TimeGenerated
columns.description: Event time when it is within the ingestion window, otherwise ingestion time.

columns.name: EventTime
columns.description: Time of the audit event as recorded by Databricks.

columns.name: SchemaVersion
columns.description: Databricks audit log schema version.

columns.name: AuditLevel
columns.description: ACCOUNT_LEVEL or WORKSPACE_LEVEL.

columns.name: AccountId
columns.description: Databricks account ID.

columns.name: OrgId
columns.description: Databricks workspace (organisation) ID; 0 for account-level events.

columns.name: WorkspaceId
columns.description: Workspace ID the event belongs to.

columns.name: ShardName
columns.description: Databricks shard (deployment) name.

columns.name: ServiceName
columns.description: Databricks service that emitted the event, for example accounts, clusters, secrets, unityCatalog.

columns.name: ActionName
columns.description: Action within the service, for example login, createCluster, getSecret.

columns.name: RequestId
columns.description: Unique request ID.

columns.name: SessionId
columns.description: Session ID.

columns.name: SourceIPAddress
columns.description: Source IP address of the request.

columns.name: UserAgent
columns.description: User agent of the request.

columns.name: UserEmail
columns.description: Email of the user or service principal that made the request.

columns.name: UserSubjectName
columns.description: Subject name from the identity.

columns.name: UserIdentity
columns.description: Full userIdentity object.

columns.name: RequestParams
columns.description: Request parameters as delivered by Databricks.

columns.name: ResponseStatusCode
columns.description: HTTP status code of the response.

columns.name: ResponseErrorMessage
columns.description: Error message when the request failed.

columns.name: ResponseResult
columns.description: Response result object.

columns.name: S3Bucket
columns.description: Reserved; populated by the Azure Function option only.

columns.name: S3Key
columns.description: Reserved; populated by the Azure Function option only.

properties.description: Detects ten or more failed Databricks login attempts from one source IP address within an hour. Repeated failures from one address against one or several accounts can indicate password guessing or credential stuffing against the workspace or account console.
properties.displayName: Databricks - Multiple failed logins from a single IP
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where ServiceName == "accounts" and ActionName has "login"
| where ResponseStatusCode >= 400
| summarize FailedAttempts = count(), TargetUsers = make_set(UserEmail, 50), Workspaces = make_set(WorkspaceId, 20),
    StartTime = min(EventTime), EndTime = max(EventTime) by SourceIPAddress
| where FailedAttempts >= 10
| extend UserEmail = tostring(TargetUsers[0])

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{FailedAttempts}} failed Databricks login attempts from {{SourceIPAddress}} between {{StartTime}} and {{EndTime}}.

properties.displayName: Databricks - Multiple failed logins from a single IP

properties.description: Detects a user or service principal being made a Databricks account admin or workspace admin, or being added to the admins group. Administrative access to Databricks grants control over clusters, data access and secrets and should be rare and expected.
properties.displayName: Databricks - Account or workspace admin privilege granted
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where ServiceName in ("accounts", "accountsAccessControl", "accountsManager")
| where ActionName in ("setAdmin", "updateRuleSet", "setAccountAdmin")
    or (ActionName == "addPrincipalToGroup" and tostring(RequestParams.targetGroupName) =~ "admins")
| where ResponseStatusCode < 400
| extend TargetUser = coalesce(tostring(RequestParams.targetUserName), tostring(RequestParams.user), tostring(RequestParams.targetUserId))
| project EventTime, WorkspaceId, AccountId, UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, ServiceName, ActionName, TargetUser, RequestParams

properties.displayName: Databricks - Account or workspace admin privilege granted

properties.description: Detects creation, modification or deletion of a Databricks IP access list, or a change to the workspace setting that enables IP access lists. Loosening these controls lets a workspace or account console be reached from addresses that were previously blocked.
properties.displayName: Databricks - IP access list or network setting changed
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where (ServiceName == "ipAccessList" and ActionName in ("create", "update", "delete", "replace"))
    or (ServiceName == "workspace" and ActionName == "workspaceConfEdit" and tostring(RequestParams.workspaceConfKeys) has "enableIpAccessLists")
    or (ServiceName == "accounts" and ActionName == "accountIpAclsValidationFailed")
| where ResponseStatusCode < 400
| project EventTime, WorkspaceId, AccountId, UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, ServiceName, ActionName, RequestParams

properties.displayName: Databricks - IP access list or network setting changed

properties.description: Detects a Databricks personal access token being created with a lifetime longer than 90 days or with no expiry. Long-lived tokens outlive the session controls applied to interactive logins and are a common persistence mechanism after an account compromise.
properties.displayName: Databricks - Personal access token created with long or no expiry
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where ServiceName in ("accounts", "tokens") and ActionName in ("generateDbToken", "tokenCreated")
| where ResponseStatusCode < 400
| extend ExpiryMs = tolong(RequestParams.tokenExpirationTime)
| extend Expires = iff(isnotnull(ExpiryMs) and ExpiryMs > 0, unixtime_milliseconds_todatetime(ExpiryMs), datetime(null))
| extend LifetimeDays = iff(isnotnull(Expires), datetime_diff("day", Expires, EventTime), -1)
| where LifetimeDays < 0 or LifetimeDays > 90
| extend TokenComment = tostring(RequestParams.comment)
| project EventTime, WorkspaceId, UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, ActionName, LifetimeDays, Expires, TokenComment

properties.displayName: Databricks - Personal access token created with long or no expiry
Databricks - Secret reads outside business hours
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ServiceName == "secrets" and ActionName == "getSecret"
| where hourofday(EventTime) !between (7 .. 19)
| extend Scope = tostring(RequestParams.scope), Key = tostring(RequestParams.key)
| summarize Reads = count(), Scopes = make_set(Scope, 20), Keys = make_set(Key, 50), FirstSeen = min(EventTime), LastSeen = max(EventTime)
    by UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, WorkspaceId
| order by Reads desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Lists reads of Databricks secrets (getSecret) between 19:00 and 07:00 UTC in the last 7 days, grouped by user and source IP. Secret reads at unusual hours from unusual addresses can indicate credential harvesting from notebooks or jobs. Adjust the hours to the customer's time zone.

properties.displayName: Databricks - Secret reads outside business hours
Databricks - Notebook exports and large result downloads
properties.query:
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActionName in ("downloadLargeResults", "downloadPreviewResults", "downloadQueryResult", "exportNotebook", "workspaceExport", "exportDirectory")
| summarize Downloads = count(), Actions = make_set(ActionName, 10), Paths = make_set(tostring(RequestParams.path), 20), FirstSeen = min(EventTime), LastSeen = max(EventTime)
    by UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, WorkspaceId
| order by Downloads desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Lists notebook exports and downloads of query or notebook results in the last 7 days, by user. A spike in exports or downloads by one user, or exports from a user who does not normally perform them, can indicate data exfiltration.

properties.displayName: Databricks - Notebook exports and large result downloads
Databricks - User activity from a source IP not seen in the previous 14 days
properties.query:
let lookback = 14d;
let recent = 1d;
let known = DatabricksAudit_CL
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(lookback + recent) .. ago(recent))
    | where isnotempty(UserEmail) and isnotempty(SourceIPAddress)
    | summarize by UserEmail, SourceIPAddress;
DatabricksAudit_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(recent)
| where isnotempty(UserEmail) and isnotempty(SourceIPAddress)
| join kind=leftanti known on UserEmail, SourceIPAddress
| summarize Events = count(), Services = make_set(ServiceName, 20), Actions = make_set(ActionName, 30), FirstSeen = min(EventTime), LastSeen = max(EventTime)
    by UserEmail, SourceIPAddress, WorkspaceId
| order by Events desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Lists users whose Databricks activity in the last day came from a source IP address not seen for that user in the preceding 14 days. New addresses are expected for mobile users and are worth checking when they coincide with token creation, secret reads or admin actions.

properties.displayName: Databricks - User activity from a source IP not seen in the previous 14 days

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The Databricks solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests the account and workspace audit logs that Databricks on AWS delivers to an Amazon S3 bucket, using the Codeless Connector Framework and Microsoft Sentinel's Amazon S3 poller. No Function App is required and no AWS access keys are stored; access uses OpenID Connect federation to an IAM role.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

  1. Codeless Connector Framework

  2. Azure Monitor data collection rules

Pre-requisites:

  1. A Databricks account on the Premium or Enterprise tier with audit log delivery to S3 configured (log type AUDIT_LOGS, output format JSON).

  2. Rights in the AWS account to deploy the two CloudFormation templates in the solution (OpenID Connect provider; IAM role, SQS queue and queue policy) and to add an S3 event notification to the delivery bucket.

Azure Databricks is not covered; it writes to Log Analytics through diagnostic settings.

Data Connectors: 1, Analytic Rules: 4, Hunting Queries: 3
